nodes.name: PtSSe Crystal Growth
nodes.procedure: Bulk crystals of PtSSe were synthesized by a chemical vapor transport (CVT). The molar ratio of Pt powder (99.99%), Se powder (99.99%), S powder (99.5%), and red phosphorus (99.999%) is 1:1.2:4:3. Red phosphorus and sulfur were the transport agents. The mixture was sealed in the quartz tube which is evacuated under a vacuum of 10^{-6} mbar. Then, the quartz tube was put and heated in a two-zone furnace. The high and low temperatures were slowly heated to 900 and 750°C, respectively. Crystal growth continued for 14 days. Finally, high-quality PtSSe crystals were fabricated in the low-temperature region.

nodes.name: PdSe2 Crystal Growth
nodes.procedure: PdSe_2 single crystals were grown in the Se-rich condition. The mass ratios were PdSe_2/Se (1:4). The source and growth temperature of PdSe_2 were 1100 and 800°C, respectively. The growth was kept for 14 days.
nodes.source_text: PdSe_2 single crystals were grown in the Se-rich condition. The mass ratios were PdSe_2/Se (1:4).

nodes.name: WSe2 Crystal Growth
nodes.procedure: WSe_2 single crystals were grown in the Se-rich condition. The mass ratios were WSe_2/Se (1:6). The source and growth temperatures of WSe_2 were 950 and 790°C, respectively. The growth was kept for 14 days.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM measures layer thickness of PtSSe flakes, showing ≈14 nm (p-type), 8 nm (intrinsic), and <8 nm (n-type) regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1a) A typical AFM image of the thickness-varying PtSSe flake on the SiO2/Si substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: SCM imaging shows n-type, intrinsic, and p-type doping regions within the same thickness-varying PtSSe flake.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b) Corresponding SCM image, showing n-type, p-type, and intrinsic doping can be realized within the same 2D PtSSe flake.

nodes.characterization_summary: KPFM shows surface potential increases with decreasing PtSSe thickness, with dC/dV response identifying carrier concentration changes per monolayer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1c) KPFM image. ... both the dC/dV response and surface potential have successfully identified an increase of the carrier concentration caused by a monolayer change (≈0.8 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM reveals 1T-type hexagonal structure with Pt vacancies in 27L PtSSe (Z-contrast profile) and anion vacancies in 8L PtSSe; lattice constants measured.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4a) STEM image of 27 layer (27L) PtSSe. Each Pt atom is surrounded by six anion atoms, showing a 1T-type hexagonal crystal structure.

nodes.evidence_snippet: When the thickness decreases, the surface potential of the layered WSe2 gradually increases, as shown in Figure 5c.
